Date: 2027-09-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Vendor consolidation evaluation — request for final recommendation

Team —

Thanks for the quick turn on the evaluation matrix and cost model. Attached is the latest cost spreadsheet and the CS requirements doc (high level). I need a concise recommendation by EOD Friday so I can present to Ops and Finance next week. Key constraints:

- Reduce number of vendor integrations where it materially lowers run cost or operational overhead.
- Preserve or improve time-to-first-response for enterprise customers (SLA targets).
- Minimize data-migration effort and legal risk (exportability + audit logs).

Quick ask: reply with a short recommendation (A: pick vendor X + reasons, B: negotiate credits, C: pilot plan) and any must-have contract clauses. I pulled current quotes from vendors (see attachments).

Attachments: cs_tooling_costs_Q3_2027.xlsx; redwood_cs_requirements.pdf

Thanks,

Date: 2027-09-05T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor consolidation evaluation — request for final recommendation

Marcus / all —

Quick take after reviewing the spreadsheet:

1) Cost: Intercom + Gainsight (messaging + success) is ~14% cheaper at current usage bands than Zendesk + Gainsight when you include add-on routing seats.
2) Feature parity: Zendesk still wins on ticketing workflow depth (Macros, multi-brand routing) and existing Zendesk apps ecosystem. Intercom is stronger for conversation-driven workflows and has a simpler product for our PLG self-serve flows.
3) Risk: Migrating historical tickets out of Zendesk is the cost driver. Data export tools exist but will need a short-term engineering sprint (2–3 weeks).

My recommendation: go with Intercom as the primary user-facing platform (lower ops friction + better chat UX) and keep Gainsight for high-touch lifecycle automation. Negotiate a migration credit from the chosen vendor to cover export/integration effort and require a 30-day data escrow clause.

Must-have clauses
- SSO + SCIM provisioning
- Data export within 30 days, machine-readable format
- Audit log retention >= 1 year (for compliance)
- SLA financial credits for P95 latency breaches

Happy to expand if you want a short slide to present.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Customer Success Operations

Date: 2027-09-07T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor consolidation evaluation — migration & legal concerns

Quick flags from procurement/infra side: 

- Data export: make sure "machine-readable" includes attachments and thread metadata; vendors often quote ticket bodies only. Require a sample export during PoC.
- Contractual: push for explicit data deletion timelines on termination and an indemnity carve-out for API rate-limits caused by vendor-side outages.
- Credits: ask Zendesk for a larger migration credit (2 months) or for Intercom to provide a free migration window.
- Integration surface: Gainsight connectors vary—confirm which fields sync out-of-the-box vs via custom transformations.

If we're leaning Intercom, I want a signed SOW for migration scope before cutover. Otherwise, for Zendesk we should request the onboarding specialist be on-site or scheduled overlap windows for the first 30 days.

-Karthik

Date: 2027-09-08T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Decision and next steps: Intercom + Gainsight (recommended)

Team —

Thanks for the fast feedback. After weighing cost, engineering effort, and our roadmap (chat-first self-serve flows are a priority), my recommendation is:

Decision
- Primary platform: Intercom for front-door messaging and conversation handling.
- Retain Gainsight for high-touch health scoring and renewal workflows.
- Decommission legacy Zendesk instance in a staged migration (export historical tickets, keep read-only archive for 12 months).

Negotiation asks
- Negotiate a 2-month subscription credit or equivalent migration services from Intercom to cover export/engineering work.
- Require SSO (SAML), SCIM, 30-day machine-readable data export (including attachments) and 12-month audit log retention in contract.
- Confirm Gainsight connector mappings for custom ticket fields; include a 4-week integration warranty in the SOW.

Immediate next steps
1) Monica: draft the short slide and exec summary for Ops/Finance review (due Monday).
2) Karthik: draft an RFP addendum with the contract clauses above and start negotiation.
3) Stephanie: schedule discovery calls with Intercom PM + Gainsight AM next week; copy engineering and security.
4) I'll notify Zendesk that we're planning a staged decommission and ask for a final export timeline and a formal migration contact.

Attachments referenced: cs_tooling_costs_Q3_2027.xlsx; redwood_cs_requirements.pdf
Related links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cCSReqs; HubSpot: HS-7562

Thanks — let's keep the decision tight and move fast.
